steps.name: 00_welcome
steps.note: The welcome screen: create an account or log in, or try a demo reader with one click.

steps.name: 01_home
steps.note: The Bookend home page: the logo shelf, Log a book, Chat w/ people, Chat w/ us, and the scrolling cover rail.

steps.name: 01b_next_book
steps.note: Your next book: the Recommendation agent ran in the background on the last book logged; below it, the shelf.

steps.name: 02_finish_form
steps.note: Alex marks Project Hail Mary finished today, 5 stars, and asks for readers from the last 30 days.

steps.name: 03_match
steps.note: Code finds 3 readers who finished it in the last 30 days (no agent needed).

steps.name: 04_host_welcome
steps.note: Alex joins the room with the Discussion Host on; the Host welcomes Alex with a question.

steps.name: 05_moderation
steps.note: One message posts; an insult is hidden by the Moderator agent; an Instagram handle is hidden by the code screen. Only Alex sees them.

steps.name: 06_priya_host_reply
steps.note: Priya's view: Alex's hidden messages aren't there. Priya mentions @host and the Host answers.

steps.name: 07_matchmaker
steps.note: Nobody finished The Remains of the Day recently, so the Matchmaker agent finds a related book with readers.

steps.name: 08_companion
steps.note: The Book Companion answers, labels its basis, and says when it is not sure instead of inventing a quote.

steps.name: 08b_chats_people_vs_ai
steps.note: The Chats tab: rooms with real people (blue) and with AI (coral) are separate, with a banner saying which one you are in, and the globe.

steps.name: 09_recommendations
steps.note: The Recommendation agent suggests real catalog books; one has readers discussing it now.

steps.name: 10_agent_team
steps.note: The agent hand-off diagram and measured tokens and cost per agent.

steps.name: 11_run_trace
steps.note: One Recommendation run expanded: each tool call, its arguments and result, and the agent's answer. Right: the moderation log.

Welcome, Alex! Jordan and Priya were just talking about how Ryland’s choice to go back changes the ending—and Jordan’s devotion to Rocky. What moment in Project Hail Mary most changed how you saw Ryland or his mission?
18:52
host_reply:
Discussion Host · AI
I’d read the book as making room for both: Ryland’s refusal is a very human act of fear, but the story doesn’t define him by it. What matters is that, with the truth in front of him, he chooses to go back—and that choice costs him something. Jordan, Priya, and Alex: did that make his return feel more heroic to you, or simply more human?

That’s the painful question at the heart of Stevens’s story. His loyalty reflects the dignity and purpose he finds in service, but it also keeps him from judging Darlington’s politics for himself—and costs him chances for intimacy and a life beyond the house. I’d say the novel invites us to see both his sincere devotion and the harm of surrendering one’s judgment to a role. What did you feel most strongly: sympathy for Stevens, or frustration with him?
